hints: Resolve all three forces horizontally: the $10\text{ N}$ force at $\alpha$ and the $25\text{ N}$ force at $60^\circ$ act in the positive $x$-direction, while the $20\text{ N}$ force at $30^\circ$ acts in the negative $x$-direction.
Set the net horizontal component equal to zero: $10\cos\alpha + 25\cos 60^\circ - 20\cos 30^\circ = 0$, and solve for $\alpha$.
Once $\alpha$ is found, resolve vertically to find the vertical component $Y$. Since the horizontal component is zero, the magnitude of the resultant equals $|Y|$.
walkthrough:
Set the horizontal component of the resultant force equal to zero:
$$X = 25\cos 60^\circ + 10\cos\alpha - 20\cos 30^\circ = 0$$
$$25(0.5) + 10\cos\alpha - 20\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 0$$
$$12.5 + 10\cos\alpha - 17.3205 = 0$$
$$10\cos\alpha = 17.3205 - 12.5 = 4.8205$$
$$\cos\alpha = 0.48205 \implies \alpha = 61.2^\circ$$

Resolve forces vertically to find the resultant (since $X = 0$):
$$Y = 20\sin 30^\circ + 10\sin 61.18^\circ - 25\sin 60^\circ$$
$$Y = 20(0.5) + 10(0.87615) - 25(0.86603) = 10 + 8.7615 - 21.6506 = -2.889\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Magnitude of resultant force} = |-2.889| = 2.89\text{ N}\text{ (downwards)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the horizontal components of the three coplanar forces:
- $10\text{ N}$ force at angle $\alpha$ above the positive $x$-axis: $+10\cos\alpha$
- $25\text{ N}$ force at $60^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis: $+25\cos 60^\circ$
- $20\text{ N}$ force at $30^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis: $-20\cos 30^\circ$

Set the net horizontal component equal to zero as given:
$$X = 25\cos 60^\circ + 10\cos\alpha - 20\cos 30^\circ = 0$$
Substitute $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$ and $\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866025$:
$$25(0.5) + 10\cos\alpha - 20(0.866025) = 0$$
$$12.5 + 10\cos\alpha - 17.3205 = 0$$
Combine the constant terms:
$$10\cos\alpha - 4.8205 = 0$$
$$10\cos\alpha = 4.8205$$
Divide by $10$:
$$\cos\alpha = 0.48205$$
Take the inverse cosine:
$$\alpha = \arccos(0.48205) \approx 61.182^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place gives:
$$\alpha = 61.2^\circ$$

Calculate the vertical component $Y$ of the forces (taking upwards as positive):
$$Y = 20\sin 30^\circ + 10\sin 61.182^\circ - 25\sin 60^\circ$$
Evaluate each term:
- $20\sin 30^\circ = 20(0.5) = 10\text{ N}$
- $10\sin 61.182^\circ = 10(0.87615) = 8.7615\text{ N}$
- $-25\sin 60^\circ = -25(0.866025) = -21.6506\text{ N}$
Sum the terms:
$$Y = 10 + 8.7615 - 21.6506 = -2.8891\text{ N}$$

Because the horizontal component $X = 0$, the resultant force acts purely vertically along the $y$-axis:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{0^2 + (-2.8891)^2} = 2.8891\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$\text{Resultant magnitude} = 2.89\text{ N}$$

hints: Substitute $\alpha = 45^\circ$ and resolve all forces horizontally and vertically to find components X and Y.
Find the magnitude using $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$ and the direction using $\tan\theta = \frac{|Y|}{X}$ below the positive $x$-axis.
walkthrough:
Calculate the horizontal component $X$ with $\alpha = 45^\circ$:
$$X = 25\cos 60^\circ + 10\cos 45^\circ - 20\cos 30^\circ$$
$$X = 12.5 + 7.07107 - 17.32051 = 2.25056\text{ N}$$

Calculate the resultant magnitude:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{(2.25056)^2 + (-4.57957)^2}$$
$$R = \sqrt{5.0650 + 20.9725} = \sqrt{26.0375} \approx 5.10\text{ N}$$

Calculate the direction angle $\theta$ below the positive $x$-axis:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{|Y|}{X} = \frac{4.57957}{2.25056} \approx 2.03486$$
$$\theta = \arctan(2.03486) \approx 63.8^\circ$$
Directed $63.8^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis (or $296^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis).
teacher_walkthrough:
Resolve the three forces along the horizontal $x$-axis when $\alpha = 45^\circ$:
$$X = 25\cos 60^\circ + 10\cos 45^\circ - 20\cos 30^\circ$$
Substitute numerical values:
$$25\cos 60^\circ = 25(0.5) = 12.5\text{ N}$$
$$10\cos 45^\circ = 10(0.707107) = 7.07107\text{ N}$$
$$-20\cos 30^\circ = -20(0.866025) = -17.32051\text{ N}$$
Sum the horizontal components:
$$X = 12.5 + 7.07107 - 17.32051 = 2.25056\text{ N}$$

Resolve the three forces along the vertical $y$-axis (taking upwards as positive):
$$Y = 20\sin 30^\circ + 10\sin 45^\circ - 25\sin 60^\circ$$
Substitute numerical values:
$$20\sin 30^\circ = 20(0.5) = 10\text{ N}$$
$$10\sin 45^\circ = 10(0.707107) = 7.07107\text{ N}$$
$$-25\sin 60^\circ = -25(0.866025) = -21.65064\text{ N}$$
Sum the vertical components:
$$Y = 10 + 7.07107 - 21.65064 = -4.57957\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force using the Pythagorean theorem:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}$$
Substitute $X = 2.25056$ and $Y = -4.57957$:
$$R = \sqrt{(2.25056)^2 + (-4.57957)^2} = \sqrt{5.06502 + 20.97246} = \sqrt{26.03748}$$
Evaluate the square root:
$$R \approx 5.10269\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures:
$$R = 5.10\text{ N}$$

Calculate the direction of the resultant force. Since $X > 0$ and $Y < 0$, the resultant vector lies in the fourth quadrant (below the positive $x$-axis):
$$\tan\theta = \frac{|Y|}{X} = \frac{4.57957}{2.25056} \approx 2.03486$$
$$\theta = \arctan(2.03486) \approx 63.829^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place:
$$\theta = 63.8^\circ\text{ below the positive }x\text{-axis}$$
(Equivalently, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis: $360^\circ - 63.8^\circ = 296^\circ$).
